facts.claim: Both `.{block-name} ...` and `main .{block-name} ...` are valid block scopes; which one fits depends on where the block is used (e.g. `main` won't match header/footer blocks rendered outside <main>, and adds specificity against global `main` rules). Don't prescribe one or flag the other as wrong.
facts.skillSays: SKILL.md:186 lists both, but the examples label `main .my-block .title` GOOD (SKILL.md:207-208) and the checklist marks `main .hero .title` as PREFERRED (references/review-checklist.md:166-169), while the checklist table says `.block-name .selector` (review-checklist.md:136).

facts.claim: commit_id is optional (defaults to the PR's latest commit); if set, use the current head SHA (`gh api repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR --jq '.head.sha'`), since an older SHA can make comments outdated.
facts.skillSays: 'Get the current HEAD commit SHA (required for review API)' (SKILL.md:582).
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request (commit_id: 'Defaults to the most recent commit in the pull request when you do not specify a value'; 'Not using the latest commit SHA may render your review comment outdated')

facts.claim: Anchor inline review comments with `line` (file line number in the diff) plus `side` (RIGHT/LEFT), not the legacy diff-relative `position`, which GitHub is closing down.
facts.skillSays: 'Use `position` (diff position) NOT `line` (file line number) - This is critical!'; troubleshooting says 'line could not be resolved' means you used line instead of position (SKILL.md:585-586, 667, 711, 948, 981).
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request ('The position parameter is closing down. If you use position, the line, side, start_line, and start_side parameters are not required'; position: 'This parameter is closing down. Use line instead'); https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request comments[] accept line/side/start_line/start_side

facts.claim: (Legacy) If `position` is used, it is counted per file: the line just below that file's first `@@` hunk header is position 1, and counting continues through later hunks until the next file; file headers and the first @@ line are not counted.
facts.skillSays: Count lines from the top of the whole `gh pr diff` output, including `--- a/` / `+++ b/` file headers and hunk headers (SKILL.md:668, 676-701, 949).
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request ('The position value equals the number of lines down from the first "@@" hunk header in the file ... The line just below the "@@" line is position 1 ... continues to increase through lines of whitespace and additional hunks until the beginning of a new file')
facts.quiz: excluded: generic and legacy; skill should drop position entirely (goal code-review)

facts.claim: `side` selects the diff side: RIGHT for added (green) or unchanged context lines, LEFT for deleted (red) lines; any line in a diff hunk can be commented, and suggestions go on RIGHT lines.
facts.skillSays: 'The position is the line number of the ADDED line you want to comment on' (SKILL.md:690, 962).
facts.verified: partial: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request (side: 'Use LEFT for deletions that appear in red. Use RIGHT for additions that appear in green or unchanged lines that appear in white and are shown for context'; default RIGHT). 'Suggestions go on RIGHT lines' follows from suggestions replacing head-branch content; not stated verbatim in docs

facts.claim: For a multi-line comment or suggestion, set start_line/start_side to the first line and line/side to the last line of the range; the suggestion block replaces the whole range, so a single-line comment's suggestion replaces only that line (don't pad it with unchanged neighbouring lines).
facts.skillSays: Never mentions start_line/start_side; says 'Include surrounding lines for context (GitHub shows ~3 lines of context)' (SKILL.md:710).
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request (line: 'For a multi-line comment, the last line of the range'; start_line/start_side 'Required when using multi-line comments'); https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/commenting-on-a-pull-request (select a range of lines, then suggest a change to 'the line or lines'). Padding duplication is inferred, not tested

facts.claim: In the JSON payload, escape newlines (\n), double quotes and backslashes, but not backticks; building the payload with `jq -n --arg` (or a script) avoids hand-escaping, and an unquoted heredoc with `\\\`` produces an invalid `\`` escape.
facts.skillSays: 'Escape special characters in JSON (quotes, backticks, newlines)'; Approach 1 example uses `\\\`ok\\\`` inside an unquoted <<JSON heredoc (SKILL.md:598-630, 671, 715, 951).
facts.verified: verified locally: the skill's `Add an \\\`ok\\\` flag` pattern in an unquoted heredoc yields `\`ok\``, and `jq .` fails 'Invalid escape'; the Quick Start body (no escaped backticks) parses. JSON spec (RFC 8259) allows only \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t \uXXXX escapes

facts.claim: Accepting a suggestion creates a commit on the PR branch with the suggester as co-author; the author can 'Commit suggestion' individually or 'Add suggestion to batch' then 'Commit suggestions' from the Files changed tab.
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/incorporating-feedback-in-your-pull-request ('Each person who suggested a change included in the commit will be a co-author'; Commit suggestion / Add suggestion to batch / Commit suggestions); applying requires write access (or maintainer edits on a fork)

facts.claim: Putting multiple suggestions in one review enables batch application.
facts.verified: partial: batching works across any suggestions on the PR regardless of which review they came from (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/incorporating-feedback-in-your-pull-request); one review mainly means one notification

facts.claim: 'Invalid commit_id' comes from using an old commit SHA; get the current HEAD SHA before creating the review.
facts.verified: partial: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request says an older SHA 'may render your review comment outdated if a subsequent commit modifies the line'; it is not itself rejected — 'commit_id' errors arise when the SHA isn't part of the PR

facts.claim: A suggestion can't be applied after a merge conflict or branch update; the author must update the branch first.
facts.verified: partial: GitHub disables applying suggestions on outdated comments (the line changed since) or on closed/merged PRs; not specifically a 'merge conflict' rule — unverified detail

facts.claim: Suggestions work in the GitHub mobile app.
facts.verified: unverified

facts.claim: Post summary comments with `gh pr comment <N> --repo owner/repo --body "..."` (use a quoted heredoc `$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)` for multi-line bodies).
facts.verified: verified: `gh pr comment --help` (--body/-b, --repo/-R)

facts.claim: `gh pr review` posts a review with --approve / --request-changes / --comment and a body.
facts.verified: verified: `gh pr review --help` (-a, -r, -c, -b/--body, -F/--body-file); note gh pr review cannot attach inline comments/suggestions, which need gh api

facts.claim: Fix commits: get headRefName/headRepositoryOwner via gh pr view --json, `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>`, check out, fix, `npm run lint`, commit, then `git push origin pr-<N>:$BRANCH` and explain the fixes in a PR comment.
facts.verified: partial: refs/pull/<N>/head fetch is valid and the JSON fields exist (`gh pr view --help`), but `git push origin ...` only works when the head branch is in the base repo; for fork PRs push to the fork (headRepository) — the computed REPO_OWNER is never used. `gh pr checkout <N>` handles both

facts.claim: Pushing fix commits needs write access; for forks, the author must have enabled maintainer edits ('usually default for same-org PRs').
facts.verified: partial: 'Allow edits from maintainers' applies only to PRs from forks in personal accounts (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork); same-repo/same-org branches need only write access

facts.claim: Fix-commit message format: `fix: <short description>`, details, list of changes, and 'Addresses review feedback: <link>'.
facts.verified: n/a: convention

facts.claim: `line` is the line number in the file (new version for side RIGHT, old for LEFT) and must fall inside one of the PR's diff hunks; GitHub rejects a line outside the diff with a 422 validation error.
facts.source: SKILL.md:948 (troubleshooting row, misattributed to using line)
facts.skillSays: 'Validation Failed: line could not be resolved' is caused by 'Used `line` instead of `position`' (SKILL.md:948).
facts.verified: partial: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request (line: 'The line of the blob in the pull request diff'; 422 'Validation failed'); exact error string not reproduced (no POSTs made)

facts.claim: To validate lines before posting, derive each file's commentable ranges from the hunk headers `@@ -oldStart,oldCount +newStart,newCount @@` (RIGHT side: newStart..newStart+newCount-1) and check every comment's line/start_line against them, with start_line < line.
facts.verified: unified diff hunk-header format (GNU diff/git); range rule follows from https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request line definition; not tested against the API

facts.claim: Leaving `event` empty creates a PENDING review that isn't visible to the author until submitted; set event explicitly (COMMENT / REQUEST_CHANGES / APPROVE).
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request ('By leaving this blank, you set the review action state to PENDING, which means you will need to submit the pull request review')

facts.claim: `gh pr review` can only post a review body with approve/request-changes/comment; inline comments and suggestion blocks require the REST endpoint (`gh api ... /pulls/<N>/reviews`).
facts.verified: verified: `gh pr review --help` (flags -a/-r/-c, -b/--body, -F/--body-file; no file/line options)

facts.claim: Pick the loading technique for third-party scripts by context rather than putting everything in the delayed phase: loadDelayed() (delayed.js / consented.js) for martech and non-critical tags, IntersectionObserver for libraries a below-the-fold block needs, load-on-interaction (e.g. click-to-load embeds/chat), or a timed loader.
facts.skillSays: Only 'Libraries via loadScript()' plus 'Consider IntersectionObserver' / 'Heavy operations use IntersectionObserver or delayed loading'.
